source.text: ወእምህየ፡ ሖርኩ፡ *ካልአ፡ መካነ፡ ምድር፡ ወአርአየኒ፡ ደብረ፡ እሳት፡ ዘያንበለብል፡ መዐልተ፡ ወሌሊተ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 printed main-text collation. Raised apparatus numbers omitted; actual asterisks, daggers and square brackets retained, including corrupt readings. translation.text: From there I went to another place on the earth, and he showed me a mountain of fire that blazed day and night.

source.text: ወሖርኩ፡ መንገሌሁ፡ ወ*ነጸርኩ፡ ሰብዐተ፡ አድባረ፡ ክቡራነ፡ ወኵሉ፡ ፩ እምነ፡ ፩ እንዘ፡ ይትዌለጥ፡ ወእእባኒ፡ *ክቡራነ፡ ወሠናያነ፡ ወኵሉ፡ ክቡር፡ ወስቡሕ፡ ራእዮሙ፡ ወሠናይ፡ ገጾሙ፡ ፫ መንገለ፡ ጽባሕ፡ ወ*ጽኑዓን፡ ፩ ዲበ፡ ፩ ወ፫ መንገለ፡ ሰሜን፡ ፩ ዲበ፡ ፩ ወቈላት፡ ዕሙቅ፡ ወጠዋያት፡ *አሐቲ፡ ለአሐቲ፡ ኢይትቃረባ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 printed main-text collation. Raised apparatus numbers omitted; actual asterisks, daggers and square brackets retained, including corrupt readings. Punctuation spacing normalized. Editor conjectures and facing Greek are not independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: I went toward it and looked at seven magnificent mountains, each different from another, with precious, beautiful stones. Their appearance was altogether splendid and glorious, and their faces were beautiful: three toward the east, firmly set one upon another, and three toward the south, one upon another. There were deep, winding valleys, which did not come close to one another.[a]

footnotes.text: Here ሰሜን has the older Geʽez sense south, not the later north: Dillmann1865 col334 gives plaga australis, meridies and explicitly contrasts the later reversal. The repeated one-upon-another construction and valleys are retained rather than supplied with a modern geographical arrangement.

source.text: ወሳብዕ፡ ደብር፡ ማእከሎሙ፡ ለእሎንቱ፡ ወ*ኖኆሙ፡ ዘይትማሰሉ፡ [ኵሎሙ፡] ከመ፡ መንበረ፡ አትራኖስ፡ ወ*የአውድዎ፡ ዕጸወ፡ መዓዛ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 printed main-text collation. Raised apparatus numbers omitted; actual asterisks, daggers and square brackets retained, including corrupt readings. Punctuation spacing normalized. Editor conjectures and facing Greek are not independent manuscript certification. The awkward plural height construction and bracketed ኵሎሙ are diplomatic, not normalized to a superlative.

translation.text: The seventh mountain was in their midst; their height resembled a throne-seat, and fragrant trees surrounded it.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected height clause has plural suffix and verbal forms, and brackets [ኵሎሙ], all of them. This English retains their height instead of silently changing it to the seventh mountain being higher than all. Charles printed p61 notes13 and47–49 discuss the difficult syntax, his changed final letter/prefixed relative, a further proposed verbal emendation, and the tentative bracketing. Those proposals are editorial, not independently checked manuscripts.

source.text: ወሀሎ፡ እምውስቴቶሙ፡ ዕፅ፡ ዘአልቦ፡ *ገሙራ፡ አመ፡ ጼነወ*ኒ፡ †ወአፄእምውስቴቶሙ፡ ወባዕዳነሂ፡ ዘከማሁ፡ አኮ፤ ይምዕዝ፡ እምኵሉ፡ መዐዛ፡ ወቈጽሉ፡ ወጽጌሁ፡ ወዕፁ፡ ኢይጸመው፡ ለዓለም፡ ወፍሬሁኒ፡ ሠናይ፡ ወፍሬሁሰ፡ ከመ፡ አስካለ፡ በቀለት።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 printed main-text collation. Raised apparatus numbers omitted; actual asterisks, daggers and square brackets retained, including corrupt readings. Punctuation spacing normalized. Editor conjectures and facing Greek are not independent manuscript certification. Full unit crosses printed60→62/PDF98→100; intervening PDF99 is facing Greek/apparatus. The initial dagger on the continuation is retained without inventing a closing sign.

translation.text: Among them was a tree whose scent I had never smelled; there was none among them, nor any other, like it.[a] Its fragrance surpassed every fragrance. Its leaves, blossoms, and wood never withered; its fruit was beautiful, and its fruit was like a cluster of dates.[b]

footnotes.text: The page-crossing clause beginning †ወአፄእምውስቴቶሙ is marked corrupt in the edition. The English no-other-like-it sense follows the surviving negative/comparison; its relationship to the smelling clause is reconstructed, not a claim that the daggered sequence is sound Geʽez. Charles p61 note16/p62 note1 discuss a missing Greek verb and a mistranslated pronoun. The source preserves the actual dagger and does not insert that proposed verb.

The selected printed *ገሙራ is interpreted with the negative temporal use of ግሙራ, never, attested explicitly for Enoch24:4 in Dillmann1865 col1147; it is not translated as a noun meaning fragrance. The smelling construction is explained at col1309; col378 explicitly cites the date/palm-cluster phrase in24:4. The printed tree/wood and repeated fruit remain distinct, not silently reduced to branches and fruit.

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ እቤ፡ ዝንቱ፡ ሠናይ፡ ዕፀ፡ ወ†*ሠናይ፡ ለርእይ፡† ወአዳም፡ ቈጽሉ፡ ወ†ፍሬሁኒ፡† ሞገስ፡ ጥቀ፡ ለርእዩ፡ ገጽ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 printed main-text collation. Raised apparatus numbers omitted; actual asterisks, daggers and square brackets retained, including corrupt readings. Punctuation spacing normalized. Editor conjectures and facing Greek are not independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: Then I said, “This tree is beautiful and lovely to look at. Its leaves are beautiful, and its fruit is very pleasing in appearance.”[a]

footnotes.text: The source daggers lovely-to-look-at and its-fruit. Charles p62 note9 prefers the facing Greek fragrant reading to the selected appearance phrase, and note10 calls fruit corrupt for blossoms. This English renders the selected appearance and fruit, not those conjectural replacements. Dillmann1865 cols937–938 cites24:5 for pleasant or delightful appearance; this does not make the corrupt textual history disappear.

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ አውሥአኒ፡ ሚካኤል፡ ፩ እም፡ መላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ወክቡራን፡ እንዘ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ሀሎ፡ ውእቱ፡ ዘዲቤሆሙ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 printed main-text collation. Raised apparatus numbers omitted; actual asterisks, daggers and square brackets retained, including corrupt readings. Punctuation spacing normalized. Editor conjectures and facing Greek are not independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: Then Michael, one of the holy and glorious angels, who was with me and was over them, answered me.

source.text: ወ*ይቤለኒ፡ ሄኖክ፡ ምንተ፡ ትስእል፡ በእንተ፡ መዓዛሁ፡ ለዝ፡ ዕፅ፡ ወትጠየቅ፡ ከመ፡ ታእምር።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 printed main-text collation. Raised apparatus numbers omitted; actual asterisks, daggers and square brackets retained, including corrupt readings. Punctuation spacing normalized. Editor conjectures and facing Greek are not independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: He said to me, “Enoch, why do you ask about the fragrance of this tree and inquire so that you may know?”

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ *አውሣእክዎ፡ አነ፡ ሄኖክ፡ *እንዘ፡ እብል፡ በእንተ፡ ኵሉ፡ እፈቅድ፡ ኣእምር፡ ወፈድፋደ*ሰ፡ በእንተ*ዝ፡ ዕፅ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 printed main-text collation. Raised apparatus numbers omitted; actual asterisks, daggers and square brackets retained, including corrupt readings. Punctuation spacing normalized. Editor conjectures and facing Greek are not independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: Then I, Enoch, answered him, “I want to know about everything, but especially about this tree.”

source.text: ወአውሥአ፡ እንዘ፡ ይብል፡ ዝንቱ፡ ደብር፡ ዘርኢከ፡ ነዋኅ፡ ዘርእሱ፡ ይመስል፡ መንበረ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንበሩ፡ ውእቱ፡ ኀበ፡ ይነብር፡ *ቅዱስ፡ ወዐቢይ፡ እግዚአ፡ ስብሐት፡ ንጉሥ፡ ዘለዓለም፡ ሶበ፡ ይወርድ፡ የኀውጻ፡ ለምድር፡ በሠናይ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 printed main-text collation. Raised apparatus numbers omitted; actual asterisks, daggers and square brackets retained, including corrupt readings. Punctuation spacing normalized. Editor conjectures and facing Greek are not independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: He answered, “This high mountain that you saw, whose summit resembles a throne, is the Lord’s throne. There the Holy and Great One, the Lord of glory, the eternal King, will sit when he comes down to visit the earth for good.”

source.text: ወዝንቱሂ፡ ዕፀ፡ መዓዛ፡ ወአልሐዱ፡ ዘሥጋ፡ አልቦ፡ ሥልጣነ፡ ከመ፡ ይግሥሦ፡ እስከ፡ አመ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ኵነኔ፡ አመ፡ ይትቤቀል፡ ኵሎ፡ ወ*ይፌጽም፡ እስከ፡ ለዓለም፤ ዝኩ፡ ለጻድቃን፡ ወለትሑታን፡ ይትወሀብ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 printed main-text collation. Raised apparatus numbers omitted; actual asterisks, daggers and square brackets retained, including corrupt readings. Punctuation spacing normalized. Editor conjectures and facing Greek are not independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: “As for this fragrant tree, no mortal has authority to touch it until the great judgment, when he takes vengeance on all and brings everything to its final end. Then it will be given to the righteous and humble.”[a]

footnotes.text: Mortal renders literally one of flesh. Humble follows selected ትሑታን rather than replacing it with a holiness adjective. The final-end expression renders the selected verb and for-ever phrase without importing a different ending from the facing Greek.

source.text: [እም]ፍሬ፡ ዚአሁ፡ [ይትወሀብ፡] ለኅሩያን፡ †ሐይወት፡† †*ወመንገለ፡ መስዕ፡† ይተከል፡ ዲበ፡ መካነ፡ ቅዱስ፡ መንገለ፡ ቤቱ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ ንጉሥ፡ ዘለዓለም።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 printed main-text collation. Raised apparatus numbers omitted; actual asterisks, daggers and square brackets retained, including corrupt readings. Punctuation spacing normalized. Editor conjectures and facing Greek are not independent manuscript certification. Full verse crosses printed62→64/PDF100→102; the intermediate facing Greek/apparatus p63 was inspected. Retains both square-bracket spans, both dagger spans and the star inside the second dagger span.

translation.text: “From its fruit, life will be given to the chosen, and it will be planted toward the north in a holy place, toward the house of the Lord, the eternal King.”[a]

footnotes.text: This is a deliberately qualified rendering of the selected, corrupt edition text. [From] and [will be given] are bracketed editorial material; life and and-toward-the-north are daggered. Charles p62 notes48–49 and p63 notes51–53 discuss interpolations and a confusion of Greek for food with toward the north, and propose changes to life and the conjunction. Those conjectures are not silently adopted here: life and north remain, and the English must not be treated as an assured reconstruction of the earlier text.

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ ይትፌሥሑ፡ በፍሥሓ፡ ወይትሐሰዩ፡ ውስተ፡ ቅዱስ፡ ወይበውኡ፡ *መዓዛ፡ ሎቱ፡ በአዕጽምቲሆሙ፡ ወሕይወተ፡ ብዙኀ፡ የሐይዉ፡ በዲበ፡ ምድር፡ በከመ፡ ሐይዉ፡ አበዊከ፡ ወበመዋዕሊሆሙ፡ ኀዘን፡ ወ*ጻማም፡ ወፃዕር፡ ወመቅሠፍት፡ ኢይገሥሦሙ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 printed main-text collation. Raised apparatus numbers omitted; actual asterisks, daggers and square brackets retained, including corrupt readings. Punctuation spacing normalized. Editor conjectures and facing Greek are not independent manuscript certification. The source has በ followed by raised Latin apparatus7, then bones; no Ethiopic numeral seven is supplied.

translation.text: “Then they will rejoice with joy and be glad in the holy place. They will enter, with its fragrance in their bones.[a] They will live a long life on the earth, as your ancestors lived; in their days sorrow, weariness, suffering, and scourging will not touch them.”

footnotes.text: The holy place supplies the place understood with selected holy. The difficult next construction is rendered with people as the continuing subject of enter, not with an unmarked causative bring. With is supplied to connect the following fragrance/bones phrase; this remains an uncertain construction, not a fully restored earlier text. Charles p64 notes5–6 discusses entering/bringing forms and interprets ሎቱ as its, reflecting a Greek genitive, rather than for him; this is an explicit syntactic interpretation, not a changed Geʽez reading. The raised apparatus reference7 after በ is not an Ethiopic seven and is excluded from the text.

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ ባረክዎ፡ ለአምላከ፡ ስብሐት፡ ንጉሥ፡ ዘለዓለም፡ እስመ፡ አስተዳለወ፡ *ለሰብእ፡ ከመዝ፡ ጻድቃን፡ ወከመዝ፡ ፈጠረ፡ ወይቤ፡ የሀብዎሙ።
source.note: Rechecked directly on Charles1906 printed64/PDF102. Source text, English and footnote text retained byte-for-byte from prior accepted individual25:7 input; only invalid footnote reason is corrected to textual_variant and source workflow metadata updated. This full-chapter successor does not erase or rewrite the prior individual review.

translation.text: Then I blessed the God of glory, the eternal King, because he had prepared such things for righteous people, had created them in this way, and said that he would give them to them.[a]

footnotes.text: The printed word order around people, such things, and righteous is unusual; this English construes righteous with people. Charles 1906 printed p64 note19 discusses that order. “Said that he would give” follows the explicit speech verb rather than introducing a separate promise formula.
